name: royal street lamp, 3/4 top-down: square stone pedestal (top face seen from above, front face with a small blue plaque), dark iron post with gold bands, an octagonal lantern with warm lit glass and a gold crown cap
label: beodeul_city/capital/capital_lamp

surfaces.part: pedestal front face with blue plaque

answer.evidence: The main body is the pedestal, rows 35-45, 12 px wide, the widest part. Its top face is a light band in rows 36-41 (L about 200-230). A darker front-edge line sits at row 42 (L=90 at x=5 and x=10), and the front face with the plaque is rows 43-45. The lantern crown is a stepped pyramid roof with widths 3, 5, 7, 9, 9 in rows 4-8 and a flat bottom edge, so it is a roof plane (c) and not an ellipse. The lantern glass is a vertical face. The post is a thin 3 px shaft. The pedestal has a visible top above a front face of 3 rows, so it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 19 visible tones per full tile, which matches prop-well-roofed (20) and prop-stall-cheese (17) and is well above prop-lamp-crook (0, a thin pole). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 50% neutral, so the outline is mixed, not a uniform black sticker line, and it sits in the same range as the bench (44%) and well (33%). The stone pedestal has a top face, a front face and a blue plaque. The post has gold bands and the lantern has lit glass and a gold cap, so the material ramps are separated by value. It is a thin object, so I judged density by eye. It is clearly richer than the crook lamp and about as dense as the other props. The ramps are slightly shallower (about 4 steps) than Beodeul's 5-6, but a careful artist would accept it beside the references.

answer.evidence: The main body is the 12px-wide stone pedestal. In column x=5 and x=10, rows 37-41 are a light band (L 170-230) that is the top face. Row 42 is a dark edge line (L=90), and rows 43-45 are the front face with the blue plaque, ending in the outline row. The top is 5 rows and the front face is 3 rows, so it reads as three-quarter, though the face is short. The lantern has a pyramid roof (rows 4-8, widths 3,5,7,9,9) over the glass (rows 9-13) and a grey base plate (rows 14-15). The roof ends flat on its lower edge, so it is a hat and not an ellipse. The post is a thin 3px vertical shaft.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin, tall prop, so I judged it mainly by eye against prop-lamp-crook, the closest reference of the same kind. It has more built structure than that lamp: a stone pedestal with a visible top face and front face, a blue plaque, a banded post, an octagonal lantern with lit glass, and a gold cap. Measured facts support this. It has 19 visible tones per tile, close to prop-well-roofed (20) and prop-stall-cheese (17), and 0% near-flat coverage. It has 24 distinct colours in total, against 14 for the crook lamp. The pedestal stone and the lantern glass each show about 4 tones, a little under the 5-6 steps in Beodeul's larger props. Dark edge pixels are 50% near-neutral, so the outline is mixed: some tinted iron and stone edges, some neutral dark ones. It is not a uniform black sticker outline, and forms are also separated by value. No large flat fills. A careful artist would accept it beside the crook lamp without it looking thinner or flatter.

Near-flat coverage is 0%, so no large flat fills. It has 24 distinct colours across stone, iron, gold, glass and a blue plaque, which is about 4-5 steps per material. Edge pixels are 50% near-neutral, so the outline is mixed: partly tinted dark tones and partly neutral dark pixels, close to the bench (44%) and well (33%) and much less of a uniform sticker line than the lamp-crook (100%). Texture is modest, with no clear grain on the stone, so it falls short of the best references but is acceptable.
